meta.title: Nujiang Coffee
meta.description: A bilingual portrait of Nujiang, Yunnan: China's high-latitude coffee frontier at 26.5°N, the Nujiang Grand Canyon, Kongque Shan, hiking trails and Nu/Lisu food.

hero.title: Where China's coffee climbs the canyon.
hero.subtitle: Most commercial arabica stops around 25°N. Nujiang grows it at 26.5°, on volcanic-ash slopes between the Gaoligong and Biluo ranges — further north than almost any coffee on Earth. The canyon is the reason: shade, altitude and a slow ripening season. This is the bean, the gorge it grows in, the trail above it and the table beside it.
hero.imageAlt: The Nujiang gorge upstream of Bingzhongluo, first snow peak at the head of the valley

coffee.title: A coffee frontier at 26.5° north.
coffee.lead: Arabica stops climbing around 25°N almost everywhere else. Nujiang grows it a full degree and a half further north, from 800 m up to 1,800 m, on volcanic-ash soil that farmers here call “panda soil”. At this latitude the cherry ripens slowly, once a year — less yield, more sugar, and a cup that reads floral rather than syrupy.
coffee.imageCaption: Coffea arabica cherries — illustrative, not shot in Nujiang

specs.label: Altitude
specs.value: 800–1,500 m (some plots to 1,800 m); the 1,200 m belt is the sweet spot

specs.label: Soil
specs.value: Volcanic-ash, selenium-rich — locals call it “panda soil”

specs.label: Climate
specs.value: High plateau, high latitude, high heat swing; distinct wet and dry seasons

industry.label: improved-variety coverage (49,800 mu of premium plots)

coffee.industryNote: Figures from the prefecture's 2025 specialty-coffee work plan and China.com.cn (Apr 2026) — full source list in the footer.

process.desc: Only fully ripe red cherries are picked; green cherries are rejected to protect the cup.
Wet-milling and raised-bed drying lock in clarity and sweetness.
Akgbi's 300 m² line now grades 1.5 t of parchment an hour — no more trucking cherry to Baoshan.
Local roasters and the “Nujiang Xiaoka” brand carry it to shelves in Beijing, Shanghai and Kunming.

coffee.tourismLead: The prefecture's coffee plan explicitly builds 咖旅融合 — coffee-plus-tourism — into estates, old towns and scenic areas.

tourism.name: Zhiziluo coffee estate
tourism.body: The “memory city” left behind when the county seat moved in 1986 now roasts beans named after Stone Moon and Crown Mountain, in an emptied 1960s street.

tourism.name: Nujiang Xiaoka 怒小咖
tourism.body: The regional public brand, shown and sold outside the province — the bean as a calling card for the canyon.

tourism.name: Lushui coffee belt
tourism.body: 349 coffee businesses and 62 cafés; estates at Lishu, Fuba and Manying host picking, processing and cupping visits.

tourism.name: Coffee & cardamom week
tourism.body: Six editions so far: a tasting fair where coffee is paired with cardamom beer, canyon food and Nu/Lisu music.

coffee.bandLine: Flavour is altitude: a slow ripening season at 1,200 m.
coffee.statement: One harvest a year. Twelve hundred metres up.

landscape.title: Two snow ranges, one river.
landscape.lead: More than 98% of Nujiang is mountain and gorge. The Nujiang (Salween) runs between the Gaoligong and Biluo ranges — a UNESCO “Three Parallel Rivers” core zone and one of the world's richest temperate ecosystems.
landscape.creditNote: All nine are photographs of Nujiang Prefecture. Place names follow the source record, not the caption writer — and where a photograph is a press image rather than an openly licensed one, the credit says so.

items.name: Nujiang Grand Canyon
items.caption: Laomden, Fugong County
items.body: Known as the “Oriental Grand Canyon”, with vertical relief exceeding 3,000 m. This is the view from the Laomden ridge, tea terraces below.

items.name: Bingzhongluo
items.caption: Bingzhongluo, Gongshan County
items.body: A farming valley of Tibetan-Buddhist, Lisu and Nu communities, and the start of the rugged Bingchacha road into Tibet.

items.name: The First Bend
items.caption: 28.00°N 98.63°E · Gongshan
items.body: The river swings around a peninsula of fields near Bingzhongluo — the gorge's most photographed turn.

items.name: Crown Mountain
items.caption: 26.56°N 98.91°E · Pihe, Fugong
items.body: The eastern wall of the gorge. Gaoligong is a biodiversity hotspot — gibbons, hornbills, thousands of plant species.

items.name: The Gongshan gorge
items.caption: 27.75°N 98.67°E · Gongshan
items.body: Upstream the gorge narrows and the road clings to the slope; the first snow peaks of the Tibetan border zone sit far behind.

items.name: Biluo cliff wall
items.caption: 26.27°N 98.87°E · Gudeng, Lushui
items.body: Bare limestone and hanging vegetation on the Biluo side — the wall that forces the river into its channel.

items.name: Gaoligong ridges
items.caption: 26.55°N 98.91°E · Pihe, Fugong
items.body: Ridge behind ridge under storm light: the vertical stacking that makes this one of the deepest gorges on Earth.

items.name: Biluo, eastern flank
items.caption: 26.11°N 98.86°E · Daxingdi
items.body: The eastern flank of the Biluo range stepping down to the river: dry, hot slopes of maize and walnut, a different world from the wet Gaoligong side.

items.name: Biluo Range & Kongque Shan
items.caption: Northern Biluo · Gongshan–Deqin border
items.body: A pyramidal peak of about 4,400 m whose ridges fall away on every side like a fanned tail — hence the name. It stands on the Gongshan–Deqin county line and separates the Nujiang from the Lancang. The old Degong road crosses at a 3,882 m pass, and the Tianxin Twelve Lakes lie in the basin just above it.

trek.title: Walk the gorge and the high lakes.
trek.lead: Two Nujiang routes made Yunnan's 2024 “Classic Hiking Routes” list. Add the alpine lakes of Kongque Shan and the old tea-horse road for a full traverse.

routes.name: Nujiang Grand Canyon (Bingzhongluo section)
routes.note: Start and end at Bingzhongluo town; passes the First Bend, a suspension bridge, Taohua Island and Puhua Monastery. On Yunnan's 2024 classic list.

routes.name: Luoguqing–Dayangchang (Lanping)
routes.note: Old-growth forest, Danxia rock peaks and alpine meadow in the Laojunshan area. On the 2024 classic list.

routes.name: Kongque Shan lakes loop
routes.note: From the pass at ~3,882 m to the Tianxin Twelve Lakes; the big loop climbs above 4,100 m toward the Cuori Laka lakes. At ~4,000 m, go slow.

routes.name: Dulongjiang secret trail
routes.note: Kongdang to the Moon Waterfall near the Myanmar border. A border-area permit is required.

trek.safety: Carry a satellite messenger, download offline maps, and never hike the gorge alone. The Dulongjiang area needs a border permit; avoid the June–September rains and check road conditions before you go.

food.title: Canyon cooking, cooked over fire.
food.lead: Nu and Lisu kitchens work with what the gorge gives: lacquer oil, stone slabs, bamboo and river fish.

dishes.name: Lacquer-oil chicken
dishes.desc: Free-range chicken braised in oil pressed from lacquer-tree seeds — the canyon's signature dish.
dishes.note: A minority of people are allergic to lacquer oil; try a little first.

dishes.name: Laowo ham
dishes.desc: Dry-cured ham from Laowo, Lushui — high-mountain pork, salt and time, no additives.

dishes.name: Stone-slab flatbread
dishes.desc: Buckwheat batter cooked on a slate slab over the fire — no oil needed.
dishes.note: A Nu and Dulong tradition from Gongshan.

dishes.name: Lisu hand-grabbed rice
dishes.desc: Rice, cured pork, roast chicken and wild greens spread on banana leaf, eaten by hand.

dishes.name: Pipa pork
dishes.desc: Nu-style cured pork, rich and marbled, sliced for guests.

dishes.name: Xiala / Gula
dishes.desc: Chicken or egg “wine stir-fry” — a warm Lisu tonic served to honoured guests.

food.allergy: Wild mushrooms must be cooked through. Lacquer oil and strong herbal wines are “slow” — go easy on your first night before a mountain day.
food.marksNote: These six dishes are drawn, not photographed. No openly licensed photograph of lacquer-oil chicken or stone-slab flatbread exists, and a picture of some other province's food captioned as Nujiang would be a lie. When we have real photographs, they go here.

visit.title: Come in the dry season.
visit.lead: The canyon is at its clearest from October to November; Kongque Shan adds rhododendron in May–July.
visit.season: Best: Oct–Nov, when water is clear and weather is stable. Spring (May–Jul) for alpine rhododendron. Avoid the Jun–Sep rains and landslide season.
visit.permits: Dulongjiang and parts of Gongshan are border areas — arrange a Border Area Permit in advance.
visit.transport: Fly or take the train to Baoshan or Lijiang, then drive in. Roads are winding; hire a local driver for the gorge.

about.eyebrow: About this build — 关于本站
about.title: A bilingual, SEO-first portal — built as a live case study.
about.lead: This site is both a portrait of Nujiang and a demonstration of the stack behind it.

problem.title: The brief
problem.body: Tell a real region's story — coffee, canyon, trail and table — to an international audience, in two languages, without turning it into a stock-photo brochure.

approach.title: The approach
approach.body: An editorial “field-notes” design: origin-specimen labels, sourced facts, and photography treated as evidence rather than decoration. Every image is geolocated to the prefecture, or explicitly marked as illustrative.

result.title: The result
items: Sourced facts with a public source list

imageRule.title: The image rule
imageRule.body: Every photograph must be placeable in Nujiang from its own metadata — a Commons category naming the county, an EXIF GPS fix, or an author description naming the village. Filenames are not evidence. Anything that fails is dropped or captioned “illustrative”, never given a Nujiang place name.
